title: Popping the front of a list
prompt:
Python 3, CPython's built-in list, holding n elements.

    items.pop()     # removes and returns the last element
    items.pop(0)    # removes and returns the first element

What is the time complexity of items.pop(0)?

Type the Big-O expression only, in terms of n - no prose, e.g. O(n log n).
reveal:
O(n). A list is a contiguous array of pointers, so removing index 0 shifts every remaining element one slot to the left. items.pop() off the end is O(1) - nothing moves.

That makes the obvious queue quadratic: draining n items with pop(0) is O(n^2). collections.deque is the fix - popleft() and appendleft() are O(1).

  items[i]            O(1)
  items.append(x)     O(1) amortized  (the backing array doubles, so the copies sum to O(n) over n appends)
  items.pop()         O(1)
  items.pop(0)        O(n)
  items.insert(0, x)  O(n)
  del items[0]        O(n)
  x in items          O(n)

The shape is the data structure's, not the language's: ArrayList.remove(0) in Java is O(n) for the same reason, and ArrayDeque is that language's answer.
